title: Biosensor for Detection of Antibiotic Resistant Staphylococcus Bacteria
protocol: Obtain type strain S. aureus ATCC 12600.
Obtain S. aureus ATCC 27690.
Obtain Bacillus subtilis ATCC 6051.
Obtain methicillin-resistant strains of S. aureus - MRSA1, MRSA 2, MRSA 5, MRSA 13, MRSA 26, MRSA 34, MRSA 45.
Obtain B. anthracis Sterne.
Obtain Salmonella typhimurium LT2.
Obtain Shigella flexneri.
Obtain Yersinia enterocolotica.
Obtain Proteus mirabilis.
Obtain Klebsiella pneumoniae 13882.
Obtain lytic phage 12600.
Obtain PBP 2a antibody conjugated latex beads.
Prepare NZY medium as described.
Obtain phosphate buffered saline solution (PBS).
Prepare deionized water for Langmuir-Blodgett monolayer deposition.
Incubate 5 ml of overnight culture of S. aureus ATCC 12600 with 500 μl of phage in 500 ml NZY medium on shaker-incubator at 37 °C overnight.
Centrifuge the culture at 4,424 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Re-centrifuge supernatant at 11,325 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Filter supernatant through a 0.22 μm Millipore filter.
Centrifuge filtrate at 75,395 x g for 1.5 hr.
Dissolve pellet in 100 μl of distilled water.
Prepare 10-fold dilutions of phage suspension in NZY medium.
Plate 1 ml of overnight culture of S. aureus ATCC 12600 onto each of 2 plates with NZY agar to cover all surface.
Remove excess culture and let the surface dry for 30 min.
Spot a sample (10 μl) of appropriate phage dilution onto the surface of the plate.
Incubate at 37 °C for 18-24 hours.
Examine the formation of plaques.
Calculate the phage titer using the formula T = N / (vxF).
Gold-immobilize quartz pieces by plasma etching in argon for 10 minutes.
Sterilize gold-coated quartz pieces under UV light for 6 hours in a sterile cabinet.
Add 50 microliters of 1 x 109 PFU/ml phage suspension to the gold surface of each piece.
Incubate overnight at room temperature in a humid chamber.
Remove and titer the remaining phage suspension after incubation.
Wash pieces with bound phage five times with PBS.
Spread an O/N culture of S. aureus ATCC 12600 onto an NZY agar plate.
Allow the plate to dry.
Place a gold piece with immobilized phage onto the plate face down.
Incubate at 37 °C for 12 hours.
Observe a zone of lysis after incubation, indicating infectivity.
Add an ON culture of S. aureus ATCC 12600 to 10 ml of NZY in each of four 300 ml sidearm flasks (6 x 10^6 CFU/ml in each flask).
Add 2 x 10^6 PFU/ml of free phage to two flasks; use the other two as controls.
Monitor the time course of S. aureus cell lysis for 570 min by optical density measurement (OD600) at 30 min intervals for all flasks.
Take a final measurement at 24 hr.
Add 50 μl of 1 x 10^9 PFU/ml phage onto the surface of sterile gold piece in a Petri dish placed into a humid chamber overnight at room temperature.
Remove the suspension with unbound phage from the gold surface and titer.
Wash the gold piece with bound phage five times with PBS.
Place the washed gold piece in 1 ml NZY solution in a 15 ml tube in shaker-incubator at 37 °C for 8 hr.
Determine the titer of detached phage as described previously.
Combine 400 μl of stock phage suspension (10^11 PFU/ml) with an equal volume of spectrophotometric grade chloroform in a 1 ml vial at room temperature.
Gently vortex the phage-chloroform suspension five to six times over one minute duration, pausing for five-second intervals between each vortexing.
Allow the suspension to stabilize for 30 sec and then pipette off the top phase containing spheroids.
Take a few microliters of the spheroids suspension for transmission and scanning electron microscopy.
Use the remaining spheroid suspension for biosensor manufacturing.
Clean QCM-D sensors by plasma etching in argon for 10 min using PDC-32G Harrick plasma cleaner.
Rinse sensor with hexane to remove any organic impurities.
Prepare and clean a trough of the film balance as described.
Fill LB trough with a subphase solution and clean it with a trough barrier.
Stabilize the trough at 20±0.1 °C.
Spread 300 μl aliquot of phage 12600 in aqueous suspension (10^11 PFU/ml) onto LB subphase.
Prepare phage monolayer by allowing 300 μl aliquot of phage 12600 aqueous suspension to run down an inclined wettable glass rod that is partially submerged into the subphase.
Stabilize the prepared monolayer for 10 min.
Compress the monolayer at a rate of 30 mm/min until a constant pressure of 19 N/m is attained.
Perform vertical film deposition onto perpendicular positioned QCM-D sensor at a rate of 4.5 mm/min by successively dipping sensor in and out of the monolayer seven times.

Repeat steps involving plasma etching, rinsing, preparing troughs, spreading phage suspension, preparing phage monolayers, compressing them, and performing vertical film deposition with a phage spheroid suspension that is prepared separately.
Use fabricated phage biosensors for MRSA detection.
Perform electron microscopy on the deposited phage monolayers before exposure to bacterial samples.
Conduct ellipsometry analysis.
Establish a base line resonance frequency of the QCM sensor in water.
Draw a suspension of live methicillin sensitive staphylococcus bacterial cells in water through the test cell.
Continuously monitor changes in the sensors resonance frequency and energy dissipation for the first overtone using Q-Soft software.
Add the suspension of PBP antibody conjugated latex beads to the flow during continuous monitoring.
Repeat steps for methicillin resistant staphylococcus bacterial cells (MRSA).
